newsitem.title: DUBAI: Omani firms in $25 mln hydrochloric acid plant.
newsitem.headline: Omani firms in $25 mln hydrochloric acid plant.

text.p: A group of mainly Omani companies plans to set up a $25 million plant to produce hydrochloric acid for the oil and gas industry, one of the project's founders said on Sunday.

National Trading Co managing director Tony Georgiou told Reuters the plant, in the Sohar industrial zone in northern Oman, would produce about 10.5 million gallons of hydrochloric acid a year when it comes on stream at end-1999.

"We are not aiming only for the Omani market, but also for the United Arab Emirates market," he said, adding that Oman's annual requirement of around five million gallons a year was currently met by imports, mostly from India.

Georgiou, speaking by telephone from Muscat, said hydrochloric acid was used in the oil and gas industry to help drill wells. The raw material for the product was salt, which would be imported either from Australia, India or Iran.
"Hal Chemicals, which have an operation at Jebel Ali in the UAE, are co-developers," he said, but added that the exact equity portion of each founder shareholder was still being finalised.
Once decided, the remaining portion would be floated on the Muscat stock exchange. "It will be open to public subscription in June or July," Georgiou said.
Construction of the plant would begin in July and take about 18 months to complete, he said.
